decades, created employment, given employment to the poor and come to the 
Parliament. So, you must give special marks. 
Now, regarding unemployment, industrialisation is more important. In the country the 
burning problem today is unemployment. The unfortunate thing is that not many new 
industries have come up. If you take the statistics for the last few decades, you will find that 
not many new industries have come up. You just verify as to how many industries have 
come up. How many new industries have come into existence? Unless there is industrial 
growth, you can't dream to solve the problem of unemployment. The permanent solution of 
unemployment is industrial growth.To have industrial growth, first red-tapism should 
be completely removed. Everywhere, in every sphere of society, in every section, 
there is red-tapism. If some entrepreneur wants something, nothing moves. The work 
which can be carried out in one day takes ten days. It is also an unfortunate thing. It is 
coming in, the way of progress. It is accelerating the quantum of poverty, the quantum of 
unemployment, the quantum of frustration and the quantum of unhappiness in the nation. 
Therefore, this is the time when our Government must plan and see how many industries 
should be established in our country. Fortunately, from 1991 onwards the licence raj and 
all that have been minimised. In spite of that, there are still problems. If you take the 
progress of the last ten years, I don't think, many industreis have come up in the country. 
The people are not able to get what they want. Some problem comes up and nothing happens. 
Therefore, a permanent solution to the problem of unemployment is industrial growth. No 
doubt, the Government will be able to provide certain temporary measures to solve the 
problem of unemployment. There are various things like Food-for-Work Programme, etc. 
They are not going to solve the problem of unemployment permanently. On the one 
side, you want agricultural production, economic growth, industrial production, growth of 
industries, etc.. To achieve this, you must sit with the industrial organisation like FICCI, Cll, 
etc., and you must verify and discuss with them what their problems are; as of today, how 
many industries are in the pipeline; to set up more industries what they want from the 
Government and various other departments and how to solve the problem of 
unemployment. Unless you have an absolute and concrete target for building up the 
nation, you can't expect any GDP growth, you can't expect any industrial growth and you 
can't expect any employment growth.

[5 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
Another burning problem is populat ion. In spite of the tremendous 
prosperity and progress in our nation, in spite of the spectacular and 
marvellous growth in various spheres and success, we are still suffering from all 
these things because of population. The growth of population is so much that 
the growth of our economy is not suffi cient. That is the major set-back. In 
olden times, in ancient times, more children in the family were considered 
good. Today, the needs are more, the education system has improved. The 
system is totally modernised and different. Today, population is the biggest 
problem for us. Today it is 102 crores and, perhaps, in a few years it may go up 
to 120 crores. The Government must take it as a challenge. In the last few years 
I did find effort that is concentrated on population control. Now, we must change 
the minds of the people, particularly, the poor people in the rural areas. The 
poor people in the rural areas have got a wrong notion. In rural areas, people 
have wrong notion that if they have more children, they would send their children 
for jobs and in the process they would earn more. This is a wrong notion. The 
Minister was also saying that there were a lot of uneducated people who feel 
that vasectomy was dangerous. They are afraid of it. Actually, there is no 
control over the increasing population, therefore, we must give training to the 
people in rural areas through the Panchayat System. You must make the 
people understand that if you have more children, you will not be able to provide 
them good education. Of course, the working class and the poor people do not 
bother about education. You have to tell them that if you have more children, 
you will not be able to give them proper health facilities, proper shelter, proper 
food, therefore, you should not have more children. It will definitely be a curse if 
you have more children. No doubt, the people in the above middle class category 
are aware of it. They are taking care of it. They are not having more than 2-3 
children. Only the people in the category of below middle class and uneducated 
people are still not aware of it. Sir, population control is interlinked with poverty, 
employment and all these factors. If you want ,   ,

effectively. How to control the population? It cannot be done by merely saying 
that you undergo vasectomy and you should not force them to go to the 
doctors. You must make the common man, uneducated man, poor man 
understand that in the modern system, it is going to be absolutely 
disadvantageous for any family to have more

women face a lot of difficulties at the time of delivery and when some poor people 
become sick, they face a lot of problems. It becomes very difficult to take them to the 
hospitals. In spite of so many schemes—I do not want to go into the details—no doubt, our 
Government is having a number of schemes and crores of rupees are being provided for the 
development of health care system, in spite of that, my question is, as my Leftist friends 
always ask, “       ?     
    ?        How are we 
going to solve this problem? Today in every village we see that the poor man is suffering 
for want of health facilities. So far as education is concerned, some people ask," What is 
the point in having higher education when there are no employment opportunities?" 
When you educate everybody, but do not give employment, that is of no use. In our 
country, we must change our education system. If you are able to get degrees in BA and 
B.Com, that are of no use. You must have such an education system that when a 
student comes out of the school, he should have an opportunity to go to the vocational 
training centers. There should be self-employment schemes for the student. So you must 
change the education system. You must know from the student in which subject they 
are intersted. If they are interested in carpentry work or electrical work or engineering 
work or any other small technical work, you must know it from them. You should introduce 
a vocational training system so that they need not depend on employment. There 
should be self-employment schemes for them. 
In summary, our education system should be modified. You must concentrate on 
the health system. You must have such a mechanism that proper health facilities are 
provided in every village, very effectively. Regarding population, we must make an effort to 
see that it is controlled fully, and that it does not grow beyond 1,000 crores, but remains at 
that.

Then, Sir, mass industrialisaton must go, and we must fully concentrate on small scale 
industries. When I said that minors' education is very important, our Left friends would

industries would help the poor man, the common man and the small graduates, But, today, it is

priority. Of course, major industries are important; when entrepreneurs come forward either 
from abroad from our own country, we must see to it that red-tapism goes off and top 
priority is given to them.

point is, to prepare a plan of action to completely eliminate poverty in the country. Action in this

point is, to prepare a comprehensive policy of interlinking rivers and make available 
safe drinking water to all. Interlinking of rivers plan is still not there. This is being

employment, etc., in each sector that has been pointed out, there is an action plan from the

manufacture enough rotis for its people. That is the irony. It is a country where we can 
build sky-scrapers, but we do not have enough small houses for our people. That is a 
fact. Similarly, in a country where we manufacture the best of textiles, we do not have 
enough clothes to cover all our people. It is a reality. We are a people who are not greedy.

SHRI MATILAL SARKAR (Tripura): I will try, but ...(Interruptions)... Thank you, Sir. I 
must congratulate the hon. Member Dr. Subbarami Reddy for having brought these issues 
by way of a Resolution in the House which conform to the basic necessities of the 
people, I should say, in the rural areas and of those people who belong to the poorer 
sections of the society. He has brought these issues for them. That is why I must thank 
him. Sir, the resolution has been brought at such a time when our Party, the Communist 
Party of India (Marxist) has given a call all over the country for launching a movement on 
the issues of land, food and employment. And this month of August is the month that we 
have selected for this movement. That is why the Resolution brought out by Dr. 
Reddy subscribes to our call. That is why I must thank him another time. Sir, while 
going into the food situation, I would like to give some reference on Indian Council of 
Medical Research. The report came in 2001 where it is stated — if I elaborate category-
wise it will take time, so I will speak in brief — the calories to be taken by the labourers 
in minimum and what they are actually taking. The difference has been shown by 
ICMR to be 13 per cent less than what the minimum requirement of K. cal. is. So, we are 
running short of 14 per cent calorie intake for rendering minimum labour for the nation. 
Sir, the National Institute of Nutrition has given a report where it is stated that in the 
drought prone areas in the country, pre-school boys and girls are suffering from 
malnutrition to the extent of 64.8 per cent in the drought-prone areas and in other 
areas the preschool boys and girls are suffering from malnutrition to the tune of 46.7 per cent 
and if we take the average, then it is sure that more than 50 per cent of the boys and girls 
and those who have not started their school studies even are suffering from malnutrition. 
They are more than 50 per cent. Sir, in the ICMR Report we see the requirement of 
milk for a person is 300 ml. here and actually he is getting 216 ml. i.e., 84 ml. short. 
In the case of eggs, the requirement of a person is 180 eggs yearly but he is getting 
only 30 eggs. He is short of 150 eggs. For meat, one needs 10.95 kgs yearly but he is 
taking only 3.2 kgs. He is short of 7.71 kgs yearly. So, what actually are the common 
people taking? From ail these statistics we see that the common people are taking 
food far short of what is required. That is why the people in the villages are 
suffering from malnutrition, suffering from want of food and suffering from availability of 
employment also. As far as work is concerned, we see that there is no work in the 
village areas at present as compared to their needs. So the 
286 

[5 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
young boys and girls and even the labourers also are rushing from villages to the cities. If we 
do not look to the villages, if do not hit upon a plan to provide work, to create work in the 
villages, if we do not take up plans to create work in the villages, in the agricultural sector 
and in horticultural sector, self-employment schemes and village industries, if then, the 
people will rush to the cities. There also they will not get any work. So, it is a very 
distressing situation for the poor people. The reason is this. During these fifty-eight years 
of bur Independence—we are going to celebrate fifty-ninth Independence Day in a 
few days from now—there is no implementation of land reforms all over the country. 
Sir, barring three or four States—West Bengal, Kerala, Tripura and a few other 
States-no State has implemented land reforms. Land is not provided to cultivators. So, 
until and unless land is given to the tiller, the basic problem of Poverty will not come to an 
end. So, the land reforms are the main task that the Government should take up. Due 
to non-availability of land, the poor people are suffering a lot and sufferings are 
multiplying each and every year. 
Sir, Mr. Reddy spoke of industries and industrialisation. He has referred to small 
industries. Yes, if the common man, living Below Poverty Line, has no purchasing 
capacity, if he cannot purchase clothes, if he cannot purchase clothes, if he cannot 
purchase soaps, if he cannot purchase pulses and if he cannot purchase the bare 
minimum necessities of the day how will the industries stand. About five-lakh small and big 
industries are now lying closed during the last five or six years. Sir, as many as, five-
lakh industries have closed down and crores of workers have lost their jobs. While we 
speak of inudustrialisation, we have to speak of economic reforms. What is the point 
there? There is an open competition. We have lifted import restrictions. About 1429 
items are now coming from abroad and are entering into our open markets. In this 
competition we see our commodities getting just staked and the market being captured by 
foreign goods. That is why our industries are closing down. This should be taken into 
account. 
I would like to raise a demand here. It is true that the Below Poverty Line families 
are getting 35 kgs. of foodgrains through Antyodaya Anna Yojana. Under this Scheme, 
poor people are getting 35 kgs. of foodgrains. Why they are getting only foodgrains? Why 
are they not getting pulses? Why are they not getting butter? Why are they not getting 
oil? Why are 
287 

RAJYA SABHA [5 A ugust, 2005] 
they not getting milk? And, why are they not getting clothes? So, my question 
is, as many as 14 to 15 items should be included in the list of ration items 
given to poor people. Each and every ration card-holder, belonging to the 
Below Poverty Line families, should be provided with 14 to 15 items which are 
of everyday necessity Without this, they cannot run their livelihood. These 
should be supplied to them through the Fair Price Shops. Giving only 35 kgs. 
of foodgrains will not suffice. My point is, the hon. Minister, while replying to this 
Resolution, should reply whether he is going to add more and more items to the 
list of commodities sold through the Fair Price Shops. This is my demand. 
Sir, I would also like to point out another thing. In our State, the State 
Government takes the wheat from the Central godowns. They grind it and supply 
the atta to the people becuase there are no milling facilities in the tribal areas and 
far off villages. But the Central Government has recently served a notice that atta 
cannot be distributed through the air price ration shops. What is this? The State 
Government grinds that wheat and supplies the atta to the people becuase there 
are no milling facilities in the rural areas. But the Central Government has put up a 
restriction that they cannot distrubute atta; they can distribute wheat only. Where 
will this wheat go if the people do not have milling facilities. This wheat will go to 
the black market; this wheat will go to the open market. What does the 
Government want to do by putting such a restriction? This restriction should 
immediately be lifted for the sake of the poor people, living in the areas where there 
are no milling facilities; where there are no flourmills. 
With these words, I conclude, Sir.

Another neighbouring State, Kerala, is more keen on allowing the water to drain Into the 
Arabian Sea, rather than sharing it with us. This is the development we have had after 
fifty-seven years of Independence! 
Another objective is, 'to prepare an action plan for providing houses to each and every 
slum dweller and those who are economically backward.' Dr Subbarami Reddy, hailing from 
Andhra Pradesh, does not seem to have visited Tamil Nadu and observed well. We have got 
a Slum Clearance Scheme. There is a Slum Clearance Board and we are providing housing 
facilities to the poor people. As far as makaan is concerned, the same is not to be seen in 
even one part of the country. We are also doing our level best at some places in the 
area of elimination of slum-dwellings. 
Then, there is mention about 'preparing an action plan to implement fully the 
educational programme initiated by the Government'. Again, taking this opportunity, I 
wish to tell this august House that in Tamil Nadu, education has been made free up to the 
school level. And, almost all the OBCs, the Schedules Castes and the Scheduled Tribes 
receive it free up to any level, even up to the level of Ph.D. Free cycle is given, free midday 
meal is given and free textbooks are given to the students, to all the students who want to 
study. Tamil Nadu is providing free cycle; free midday meal, free textbooks and Tamil 
Nadu can be taken up as a role model for this. 
Prepare a plan of action to provide employment to each and every citizen of this 
country. Sir, this can be achieved not by multinational companies coming in and beating 
the people as we have seen recently in Haryana. This can be done only by encouraging 
small-scale and cottage industries. But what is happening? Due to free trade, Coca-Colas 
have come, Fantas have come, and, we have eliminated our local brands. This is the 
achievement that we have made in these 57 years. 
We have to impove in the agriculture sector, which has started showing declining trends. 
There is no proper distribution of water and this is the main reason. It would be better if 
we could improve agriculture in this regard. Recently, there have been rains in Godavari 
area and it is stated, just three days ago, it appeared in all the newspapers, that water required 
over 12 years in that area has been wasted in the sea for want of proper dams and check 
dams to be build. This is the level of progress that we have done. We should be ashamed 
that we have not ruled well ourselves.

Sir, the next point deals with health centres. There is common cry almost all over 
India that doctors are not willing to work in rural areas. That issue can be sorted out. I have 
a suggestion here. We are subsidising medical education. The cost of a doctor's education is 
incurred from public exchequer. He can be asked to execute a bond or a guarantee letter at 
the time of his entry into the medical college that he will definitely serve in rural areas for at 
least 2-5 years after completion of his course, failing which he will refund a certain amount 
of money, which the Government spent on him. Because the amount he pays for his 
education does not satisfy the entire expenditure of education. Like that, by bringing 
forward a legislation or by bringing forward an authority to that extent, we can compel 
students, who are entering into medical colleges, to serve definitely for a particular period in 
rural areas. That way, we can encourage them to work in rural areas. Otherwise, there 
will be more doctors in urban areas and there will be no doctors in rural areas. This can 
be sorted out in that way. 
Lastly, I come to the ninth command ment. Instead of ten commandments, 
my friend mentioned nine commandments. It says, "prepare an economic policy to 
ensure its proper implementation with more Foreign Direct Investment." Sir, again, it is 
a myth. Nowadays Foreign Direct Investment is quite often discussed. The Foreign 
Direct Investment has not brought any harmony to this country. Rather it has killed Small 
Scale Industries and Cottage Industries. We must have a rethinking on Foreign Direct 
Investment. It comes only in soft drinks. That is the biggest area where we have 
attracted more Foreign Direct Investment. Sir, people are not getting frustrated; on the 
contrary, they are in the greatest anger. They are very angry over the governance of this 
country. If you want to curtail this and keep them in good humour, you must change your 
policies and you must rule well and better. Thank you, Sir.
